stem: For an adolescent with frequent daytime symptoms on most days and waking overnight more than once a week, what is a recommended initial treatment?

options.text: Short-acting beta agonist (SABA) alone as needed.
Medium to high dose inhaled corticosteroids plus as-needed SABA.
A trial of Montelukast alone for 4 to 6 weeks.

explanation: High symptom frequency in adolescents necessitates a more aggressive starting point with medium to high dose ICS or maintenance combination therapy.
rationale: High-frequency symptoms in teenagers require a higher starting tier of inhaled preventer therapy.

optionExplanations.A: SABA alone is only appropriate for very infrequent symptoms in adolescents.
optionExplanations.B: High symptom frequency in adolescents necessitates a more aggressive starting point with medium to high dose ICS or maintenance combination therapy.
optionExplanations.C: With symptoms on most days, Montelukast alone is likely insufficient as an initial therapy.
optionExplanations.D: Oral steroids are used for short bursts (3-5 days) to manage acute flares, not as a standard long-term initial preventer strategy.
